Shri K.S. Kaurav - learned counsel for the respondents  ORDER

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred by the appellant against the award dated 30.01.2011 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (FastracK), District Shyopur in Claim Case No.13/2010 whereby MACT has awarded an amount of Rs.2,52,591/- alongwith interest @ 6%
per annum in favour of the respondent No.1/claimant.

entities.text: Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (FastracK), District Shyopur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 . The necessary facts for the disposal of this appeal are that on 23.2.2008, when Naval Kishor was going on motor cycle, an Auto bearing registration No. R.J.-20-T-3936, which was being driven by respondent No.2 - Shareef in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle due to which he sustained grievous injuries.

3 . Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submits that learned Tribunal has found proved that no valid and effective driving license was possessed by the driver of the offending vehicle and therefore, there was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14214 2 MA-792-2011 a breach of insurance policy.

Learned Tribunal, on the basis of breach of the condition of insurance policy, has rightly directed that after making payment to the claimant, the insurance company is entitled to recover the awarded amount from the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
Such 'pay and recover' order ought to be issued in respect of permit also.
The permit was also required to be possessed by the owner of the offending vehicle.
The insurance company has filed an application before the learned Tribunal under Order XI Rule 12 of C.P.C. for production of the permit of the offending vehicle before the Tribunal.

However, the driver of the offending vehicle in his reply dated 1.10.2010 has categorically stated that the offending vehicle bearing registration No. R.J.-20-T-3936 was not being used as a transport vehicle and therefore, no transport permit was necessary for such vehicle.

In the light of the reply, the application under Order XI Rule 12 of C.P.C. was not pressed by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company as recorded in the order dated 12.10.2010 passed by learned Tribunal.

However, such an admission shows that on the date of New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Nawalkishor on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154303630/
1 accident no permit was available with the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: It ought to be concluded by the learned Tribunal while deciding the issue No.3 that in the absence of permit of offending vehicle, there is a breach of policy conditions; therefore, 'pay and recover' principle is applicable in respect of the permit as well.
4. Per contra- learned counsel for the respondent/claimant has opposed the application and prayed to dismiss this appeal.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it is found that the Insurance Company has filed an application under NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:14214 3 MA-792-2011 Order XI Rule 12 of C.P.C. before the learned Tribunal for getting the permit of the offending vehicle produced before the learned Tribunal.
However, the same was denied in the reply by the driver of the offending vehicle on the ground that a transport permit is not required for a vehicle, not being used as a transport vehicle.

The vehicle in question is an auto bearing registration No.RJ-20-T3936, used for carrying passengers or goods; therefore, as per the provisions of Section 66 of the Motor Vehicles Act, a permit was necessary for using the vehicle.

In the absence of a permit, if the vehicle was being used, then it would be in contravention of the conditions of the policy marked as Ex.D/2.
6.

Though, the learned Tribunal has found it proved that the offending vehicle was being driven by driver in violation of condition of policy in issue No.3 in the absence of valid and effective driving licence but keeping in view the reply dated 1.10.2010 on behalf of the driver of the offending vehicle it is clear that there was no permit as well in respect of the offending vehicle and that is another ground of breach of condition of the policy available with the insurance company.
7. No other grounds have been agitated by the insurance company; therefore, this appeal has been disposed of with the observation that issue No.3 is found proved also in respect of absence of permit.

The insurance company is rightly directed by the learned Tribunal to first pay the compensation amount to the claimant, thereafter, it shall be at liberty to recover the same from the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.

8. Consequently, while maintaining the impugned award, the observation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14214 4 MA-792-2011 of learned Tribunal on issue No.3 is hereby modified to the extent that there was a violation of the condition of insurance policy in respect of absence of both the driving licence and the permit of the offending vehicle.
9. In view of the aforesaid, this appeal is disposed of .

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE Ahmad New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Nawalkishor on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154303630/
